summary.headline: Escorts Kubota Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28% to INR3,178.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.2% from 13.1% on commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from continuing operations grew 28% YoY to INR3,178.9 crore, with tractor domestic volume at a record 35,457 units (+22.9%) and market share up 36 bps. Standalone EBITDA rose 9.4% to INR355.4 crore, but margin compressed 190 bps to 11.2% as metal and rubber commodity inflation (about 5% on tractors per management) hit costs. Net profit growth of 4% reported is distorted by a INR76 crore land-sale gain and RED divestment in the base quarter; management cites 26% growth excluding the gain. Management raised its FY27 industry outlook to mid-to-mid-single-digit growth from a prior plus/minus 2-3% view, and flagged a further 1.5-2% cost pressure in Q2 with price hikes under discussion.

financial_highlights.change: +4% YoY; +26% excluding prior-year INR76 crore land-sale gain

segments.name: Tractors (domestic)
segments.commentary: Sold 35,457 units, record Q1 and +22.9% YoY vs industry +18.6%, gaining 36 bps share. South industry grew about 33% (overall 19%); Escorts South share about 6% after ~0.5-0.6 pp gain.

segments.name: Tractor exports
segments.commentary: Exports fell to 1,405 units from 1,733 (down about 19%) while industry exports rose 17.7% to 29,778; vessel availability and weak sub-40 HP compact exports (down ~8%) hurt. Kubota global network accounts for ~61% of export volume.

segments.name: Agri Machinery non-tractor business
segments.commentary: Agri Solutions, engines and spares/service parts were 19% of Agri Machinery revenue vs 18% a year earlier. Component exports were flat in Q1 and about INR160-170 crore last year.

segments.name: Construction Equipment
segments.commentary: Volume 1,344 machines (+27.4%) and revenue INR419.6 crore (+39.2%); EBIT impacted by commodity inflation. Crane industry grew 46% in Q1, partly on a low BS-V-affected base.

guidance_outlook: Domestic tractor industry FY27 now guided to mid-to-mid-single-digit growth (previously plus/minus 2-3%); Escorts expected to outgrow the industry via share gains.
Tractor cost pressure of about 5% continues in Q2 with a further 1.5-2% expected; management expects reversal from Q4 if geopolitical situation eases.
Price increases under discussion, not finalised; management said they will not fully offset material cost increases.
Tractor exports expected roughly flat in FY27 with Q1 shortfall recovered over the remaining three quarters; FY28 growth expected, including potential North America entry.
Construction equipment industry FY27 growth 12-15%: mini excavators and cranes high, backhoe loaders 5-7%, compactors 5-6%. Escorts CE expected to grow 12-15% for the full year.
FY27 capex INR850-900 crore: INR450-500 crore greenfield land (groundbreaking expected this month) plus INR350-400 crore normal capex. Total greenfield project INR2,000 crore.
Captive finance penetration 10-12% of dealers in Q1, nearing 15% in July; 40-50% of dealerships targeted by FY27 and pan-India by FY28.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex of INR850-900 crore: greenfield land INR450-500 crore (already paid, development starting) and normal capex INR350-400 crore.
Greenfield project total outlay about INR2,000 crore; FY28 spend could rise if construction is accelerated on strong demand.
Dealer channel holds about 30 days of inventory; company plans to build stock ahead of the festive season, which management says starts later this year from October.
Construction equipment: new models from October, and BS-V versions of backhoe loaders and compactors from September.
Captive finance covers limited states with about 250 dealers onboarded; southern states to be added in FY27.
demand_pricing: Industry record Q1 tractor volume of about 3.39 lakh units; management expects demand upside vs earlier guidance, with the last 45-50 days described as very positive.
Q2 growth may slow against a high base and the late festive season; monsoon distribution is the key monitorable.
Tractor price hike of about 1-1.5% taken in April; further hike being evaluated for Q2.

Construction equipment: cumulative price increases of about 6% effective (after channel discount adjustments) passed on in small tranches since the January 2025 BS-V hike; customers are negotiating longer, and prices are expected to stabilise in Q2.
Product gains: Promaxx contributes 20-22% of Farmtrac sales; Digitrac (incl. new 4x4) contributes 23-25% of Powertrac portfolio. Gap remains in 35-50 HP 4WD segment for Powertrac.
Escorts estimates Haryana contract-labour wage increase accounts for about 1% of the tractor cost impact.
